req.title: Index renders even with zero posts
req.statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-037 requires the index page (GET /) to render successfully with HTTP 2xx even when the post table is empty. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — empty DB, verify HTTP 200 and that the response body does not contain any post content from the pre-loaded fixture, confirming empty-state rendering; (2) negative — verify that when posts DO exist (pre-loaded fixture), the response still returns 200 but contains post data, confirming the empty-state path is distinct from the populated path (NEG: wrong branch); (3) boundary — the transition from zero posts to one post and back to zero, verifying the exact status code 200 at the zero-post boundary (BVA). All tests use exact status code assertions and content checks to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_index_empty_db_returns_200
preconditions: Database is initialised with schema but NO rows in the post table
actions: Create a fresh app with an empty temporary database (init_db called, no posts inserted)
expected: Response body does not contain 'test title' (the pre-loaded post title)
trace: R-FLASKR-037: index renders even with zero posts -> HTTP 2xx response
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_index_empty_db_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
        with app.app_context():
            init_db()
        client = app.test_client()
        r = client.get('/')
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert b'test title' not in r.data
        assert len(r.data) > 0
    finally:
        os.unlink(path)

test_index_empty_db_returns_200()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

def test_index_with_posts_returns_200_and_post_content():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
        with app.app_context():
            init_db()
            db = get_db()
            db.execute(
                'INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)',
                ('test', generate_password_hash('test'))
            )
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                ('test title', 'test\nbody', 1, '2018-01-01 00:00:00')
            )
            db.commit()
        client = app.test_client()
        r = client.get('/')
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert b'test title' in r.data
    finally:
        os.unlink(path)

test_index_with_posts_returns_200_and_post_content()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

def test_index_boundary_zero_posts_exact_status():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
        with app.app_context():
            init_db()
            db = get_db()
            count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
            assert count == 0
        client = app.test_client()
        r = client.get('/')
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 500
        assert len(r.data) > 0
        assert b'test title' not in r.data
    finally:
        os.unlink(path)

test_index_boundary_zero_posts_exact_status()

tests.name: test_index_transition_post_deleted_returns_200
preconditions: Post is then deleted, leaving zero posts
actions: Create app, init DB, insert one post
Verify GET / returns 200 with post content
Delete the post from DB directly
Verify GET / still returns 200 and post content is gone
expected: First GET /: status 200, b'test title' in response
After deletion GET /: status 200, b'test title' NOT in response

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

def test_index_transition_post_deleted_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
        with app.app_context():
            init_db()
            db = get_db()
            db.execute('INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)',
                       ('test', generate_password_hash('test')))
            db.execute("INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                       ('test title', 'test\nbody', 1, '2018-01-01 00:00:00'))
            db.commit()
        client = app.test_client()
        r1 = client.get('/')
        assert r1.status_code == 200
        assert b'test title' in r1.data
        with app.app_context():
            db = get_db()
            db.execute('DELETE FROM post WHERE title = ?', ('test title',))
            db.commit()
            count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
            assert count == 0
        r2 = client.get('/')
        assert r2.status_code == 200
        assert b'test title' not in r2.data
        assert len(r2.data) > 0
    finally:
        os.unlink(path)

test_index_transition_post_deleted_returns_200()
